design: A CHACMOOL: a Mesoamerican stone sculpture of a reclining figure lying on its back with knees raised, propped on its elbows, its head turned to face the side, holding a round shallow stone dish on its stomach (an offering vessel) with a few yellow marigold flowers in it; carved from grey stone with traces of red and blue-green paint. Calm and dignified.
see: a stone statue of a reclining figure holding a dish

desc: stone altar with offerings
hint: the far wall of a temple shrine
design: A Mexica stone ALTAR: a broad low rectangular block of grey stone, its sides carved with a band of stepped fret and painted red and ochre, its top laid with OFFERINGS: ears of yellow and red maize, a heap of orange marigold flowers, painted clay bowls and a three-legged clay incense burner with a lump of white copal resin. No blood, no knife, nothing grim.
see: a stone altar covered with maize, flowers and bowls

desc: great painted ceramic brazier
hint: flanking the altar of a shrine; a palace hall
design: A great Mexica ceramic BRAZIER: a big round fired-clay brazier bowl on a tall flaring pedestal, waist high, painted ochre with a band of red and black geometric pattern and two big knobs on its rim, its bowl filled with black charcoal. It is COLD and UNLIT: dull charcoal and pale ash, NO flames, NO glow, NO smoke (the game adds the fire).
see: a large painted clay fire bowl on a pedestal

desc: ballcourt sloping bench wall section
hint: the two long sides of a ballcourt
design: One 10-ft section of a Mesoamerican BALLCOURT side: a long massive stone BENCH with a steeply SLOPING face toward the playing alley, rising to a short vertical wall at the back, plastered smooth and painted cream-white with a red band along the foot of the slope. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a long stone bench with a sloping face

desc: ballcourt wall section with the stone ring
hint: the middle of each long side of a ballcourt
design: The same ballcourt side section: a long stone bench with a steeply SLOPING plastered face rising to a vertical wall at the back, and set HIGH in the middle of that wall a big carved STONE RING standing upright (its hole facing across the court), the ring carved with a band of feathers; cream-white plaster with a red band at the foot. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a sloping stone wall with a big stone ring set upright in it

desc: a lord's backed seat of woven reeds (icpalli)
hint: the far wall of a noble's house
design: A Mexica lord's SEAT (icpalli): a low seat of tightly woven golden reeds with a high slanted back, the back taller than the seat is wide, covered with a spotted jaguar-pattern cloth (painted, not real fur) over the seat and a woven cotton border in red. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a low woven reed seat with a high back

desc: woven reed chest (petlacalli)
hint: a noble's house; a scribe's room
design: A Mexica PETLACALLI: a rectangular lidded chest woven of golden reed matting in a twill pattern with a dark red woven border, tied shut with a thick cotton cord. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a woven reed box with a lid

desc: grinding stone (metate) with mano
hint: the kitchen side of a house
design: A Mesoamerican METATE: a slab of grey volcanic basalt on three short stout legs, its top dished, sloping toward the front, with a long cylindrical stone MANO (hand stone) lying across it and a little heap of yellow maize dough on the slab. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a stone grinding slab on three legs with a stone roller

desc: three-stone hearth with a clay griddle (comal)
hint: the cooking place of a house
design: A Mesoamerican HEARTH: three rounded grey hearthstones set in a triangle on the ground holding a big round flat clay griddle (comal), with three tortillas on it and a little black charcoal under it, a clay cooking pot beside the stones. It is COLD and UNLIT: dull charcoal and pale ash, NO flames, NO glow, NO smoke (the game adds the fire).
see: three stones holding a round flat clay griddle

desc: painted water jar on a ring stand
hint: a house; a courtyard
design: A big round-bellied Mexica water JAR of orange fired clay painted with black and cream bands and a stepped-fret band round the shoulder, with a narrow neck, sitting on a thick woven reed ring. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a round painted clay water jar

desc: a vendor's mat heaped with maize
hint: a market plaza, in rows
design: A market VENDOR'S SPREAD: a square woven reed mat on the ground with goods on it: two big round baskets heaped with yellow and red ears of maize, a heap of loose dried maize cobs and a basket of black beans. The things on it are FEW and BIG, packed tight as solid masses (nothing tiny, nothing floating).
see: a mat on the ground with baskets of maize

desc: a vendor's mat of chilies, beans and squash
hint: a market plaza, in rows
design: A market VENDOR'S SPREAD: a square reed mat on the ground with low baskets heaped with bright RED dried chili peppers, brown beans and pale green squash gourds, with a small pyramid of squash at one corner. The things on it are FEW and BIG, packed tight as solid masses (nothing tiny, nothing floating).
see: a mat with baskets of red chilies, beans and squash

desc: a potter's spread of jars and bowls
hint: a market plaza, in rows
design: A market VENDOR'S SPREAD: a square reed mat on the ground set out with orange and black painted clay pots, tripod bowls, griddles stacked on edge and two big jars, arranged in tight groups. The things on it are FEW and BIG, packed tight as solid masses (nothing tiny, nothing floating).
see: a mat with painted clay pots and bowls

desc: a weaver's spread of cotton mantles
hint: a market plaza, in rows
design: A market VENDOR'S SPREAD: a square reed mat on the ground with folded cotton mantles (tilmatli) stacked in neat piles, white with bold red, black and ochre geometric borders, and one mantle spread open on top showing its pattern. The things on it are FEW and BIG, packed tight as solid masses (nothing tiny, nothing floating).
see: a mat with stacks of patterned folded cloth

desc: cotton shade awning on four poles
hint: over a vendor's spread in a market
design: A market SHADE AWNING: a flat rectangle of undyed cotton cloth with a red striped border stretched taut on four THICK upright wooden poles about 8 ft tall, tied at each corner; nothing under it. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a cloth awning on four poles

desc: raised chinampa bed with maize
hint: the fields of a chinampa garden, in rows
design: A CHINAMPA bed: a long raised rectangular garden plot of dark rich earth about 15 ft long and 4.5 ft wide, edged with a woven reed and stake kerb, planted with two rows of tall green MAIZE plants with yellow tassels, the plants packed as one solid green mass. Foliage is a FEW big solid masses with broad leaf shapes painted on them, never separate thin leaves or twigs; no gaps you can see through, nothing floating free.
see: a long raised garden bed with rows of corn plants

desc: dugout canoe (acalli)
hint: the canal of a chinampa garden
design: A Mexica dugout CANOE (acalli): a long narrow flat-bottomed boat carved from one log, about 14 ft long, square-ended and low, honey-brown wood, a long wooden pole and a paddle lying in it with a basket of maize. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a long narrow dugout canoe

desc: ahuejote willow tree
hint: the edges of chinampa beds
design: An AHUEJOTE willow: a tall, very narrow upright tree about 18 ft tall, its silvery green foliage one tight slender column from near the ground to the top, a short pale trunk at its foot. Foliage is a FEW big solid masses with broad leaf shapes painted on them, never separate thin leaves or twigs; no gaps you can see through, nothing floating free.
see: a tall narrow willow tree

desc: a scribe's paint pots and brushes on a mat
hint: a scribe's room, beside the codex
design: A Mexica SCRIBE'S paint set on a small reed mat: six small round clay pots of thick paint (red, black, ochre, white, turquoise, green), a few thick reed brushes lying beside them and a stack of folded blank bark paper. The things on it are FEW and BIG, packed tight as solid masses (nothing tiny, nothing floating).
see: small pots of coloured paint and brushes on a mat

desc: roof-support post of a longhouse
hint: two rows down a longhouse or hall, either side of the hearth
design: One round timber ROOF-SUPPORT POST of a Viking longhouse: a thick round oak post about 9 ft tall and as thick as a man's thigh, standing straight on a flat foot stone, its top cut square to take a beam, a band of carved interlace round it at head height; weathered grey-brown wood. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a tall thick wooden post

desc: octagonal marble floor fountain
hint: the middle of a qa'a, a hammam's cool room or a courtyard
design: A Mamluk FLOOR FOUNTAIN (fisqiya): a low OCTAGONAL basin of white marble set into the floor, knee high, about 5 ft across, its rim and the floor panel round it inlaid in a geometric pattern of red, black and white marble, a small stepped marble jet-stand in the middle; the basin holds shallow, pale, LIGHT TEAL water, painted flat and clear.
see: a low octagonal marble fountain basin with water

desc: marble bench (mastaba) of a bath
hint: along the walls of a hammam
design: A hammam MASTABA: a long low built-in bench of white and pale grey veined marble slabs about 8 ft long and knee high along a wall, its front panelled, a folded striped cotton bath towel and a pair of tall wooden bath clogs on it. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a long low white marble bench

desc: khan arcade bay with a storeroom door
hint: round the court of a caravanserai (its edge)
design: One BAY of a caravanserai (khan) arcade, as a building kit piece 5 ft wide: a pointed stone ARCH on two square piers at the front, a short vaulted passage behind it about 6 ft deep, and at its back a plain stone wall with one small dark storeroom doorway; honey-coloured limestone with a dark ablaq course, a flat roof slab on top. Both side edges cut clean so bays butt together into a long arcade. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a stone archway bay with a doorway at the back

desc: square stone pier closing an arcade
hint: the corners and ends of a khan arcade
design: One square stone PIER about 2 ft square and 11 ft tall, honey limestone with a band of dark ablaq stone at its foot and a plain moulded capital at the top. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a tall square stone pillar

desc: great gateway of a khan
hint: the street side of a caravanserai court
design: The GATEWAY of a caravanserai, as a kit piece 5 ft wide: a tall pointed-arch portal in honey limestone with striped dark and light arch stones, a carved band of stepped honeycomb (muqarnas) in its hood, and a pair of heavy wooden gate leaves studded with iron standing wide OPEN against its sides. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a tall stone arched gateway with open wooden gates

desc: plank gate of a fenced yard, with its little roof
hint: the street side of a stockade yard
design: The GATE of a Rus' fenced yard compound, as a kit piece 5 ft wide: two massive squared gateposts carrying a small pitched plank roof across their tops, and between them a pair of heavy plank gate leaves standing OPEN; weathered golden-brown wood, a simple carved board under the little roof. Built CHUNKY for a tabletop miniature: every post, leg, rail, handle and pole is THICK, at least as thick as a man's arm; nothing thin, no wire, no string, no loose dangling parts.
see: a wooden gate under a little roof

desc: screenfold codex unfolded on a reed mat
hint: the middle of a scribe's room
design: A Mexica SCREENFOLD CODEX laid open on the floor: a long strip of white-plastered bark paper folded like a fan, several pages unfolded flat side by side on a woven reed mat, a low woven cushion at one side where the painter kneels. The pages are painted in the manner of the Codex Borbonicus: day-sign pictures in coloured boxes on white, framed by red guide lines (pictures, no letters). The things on it are FEW and BIG, packed tight as solid masses (nothing tiny, nothing floating).
see: a long folded painted book spread open on a mat

desc: woven cotton door curtain
hint: hangs in a Mexica doorway (no hinged doors)
design: A DOOR CURTAIN as a stiff hanging panel: a heavy woven cotton cloth about 3 ft wide and 6.5 ft tall hanging straight and flat from a thick wooden rod, cream with broad red and black stepped-pattern bands across it and a fringed bottom edge. Flat and upright like a door leaf, about 3 in thick.
see: a flat woven striped curtain hanging from a rod
